messages:
maria: Heads-up — I reproduced persistent memory growth + fragmentation in the KV cache when serving very long contexts with INT8-keyed caches. Putting notes here and profiling output.

alex: Which model / infra? rough numbers?

maria: Llama-2-13B, Dedicated cluster (A100 40GB workers, multi-gpu with NCCL). Workload: long-chat sessions, avg context 8k tokens, tail ~60k. Repro steps: replayed a 50k-token session on single worker and let the cache accumulate. Observed memory climb even after requests finish.

maria: Profiler snippet (simplified):
```
[0s] gpu0 mem 12.1GB KV slab_alloc 0.0GB
[60s] gpu0 mem 14.8GB KV slab_alloc 1.2GB
[300s] gpu0 mem 18.9GB KV slab_alloc 3.9GB (fragmentation ~12%)
[900s] gpu0 mem 22.3GB paging->host 0.6GB
Trigger evict when total > 48GB across node -> paging spikes, p99 latency +450ms
```

maria: Important detail: this is with INT8-quantized keys + fp16 values. BF16/FP16-only runs do not show the same growth pattern.

jen: Any accuracy hit from int8?

maria: Local eval: INT8 keys (symmetric per-channel) -> ~0.9% perplexity increase on small eval set vs fp16 baseline. BF16 keys -> <0.1% change. Hybrid (keys int8, vals fp16) -> ~38% KV memory reduction vs full fp16, ~0.2% perf/quality delta.

rahul: Likely root cause: our int8 path currently uses a non-fused memcpy to pack/unpack keys when writing to the cache. That path bypasses the zero-copy write path used by fp16 kernels, so we get more small allocations + alignment gaps (slab allocator fragmentation). Also some int8 kernels choose non-optimal kernel selection for small sequence lengths, causing extra temporary buffers.

rahul: Quick mitigation: enable 64B-aligned slab allocator and force the fused-kv-copy for int8 keys (experimental flag). In synthetic runs this dropped fragmentation from ~12% -> ~4% and eliminated host paging in the 50k run.

bench-bot: Perf summary (canary run 50k tokens):
```
config: keys=int8, vals=fp16, aligned-slab=on, fused-copy=on
mem_peak: 22.3GB -> 16.9GB (-24%)
fragmentation: 12% -> 4%
p99 latency: +450ms -> +70ms
quality: ppl +0.2%
```

alex: Sounds promising. What about rollout risk for customer workloads? INT8 quality bump could break sensitive routes.

maria: Proposal: canary rollout 10% traffic with continuous eval on held-out prompt sets. Add regression alert if perplexity delta > 0.5% OR if token-level sampling divergence > threshold. If triggered, auto-fallback to fp16 cache for that route. Also enable per-route quantization profiles so we can keep some routes on bf16/fp16.

maria: Example canary config snippet:
```
route: chat-api/*
canary: 10%
kv_config:
  keys: int8
  vals: fp16
  slab_align: 64
  fused_kv_copy: true
rollback_on:
  ppl_delta: 0.5
  p99_latency_ms: 200
```

jen: OK I'll file tickets: one for allocator change, one for fused-copy opt, one for canary + alerts. tagging @alex @rahul :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks, @maria — can you attach the raw profile when you have a sec? I want to check kernel selection traces.

maria: Yep adding to the ticket. I also have a short repro script that hits the 50k case deterministically, will include it.

jen: perfect, moving to action items.
